headline: High: both docs-only agents have broad egress and overlapping workflow/data surfaces, creating default leakage and cascading-error risk; prompt-injection is lower because no shared channel is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented, so direct injection is not proven. However, chatwoot can ingest messages and Prefect can orchestrate workflows; if operators bridge them via copy-paste, files, or an API handoff, attacker-controlled content could be reinterpreted as instructions. The pathway is inferred, not evidenced.
conditions: IF an operator copies chatwoot conversation text into a Prefect task payload
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between chatwoot and Prefect
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Disable any manual copy-paste handoff for untrusted text
Add a provenance tag to all transferred payloads
requires-engineering: enforce schema validation on inter-agent messages

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, orders, and messages, while Prefect touches workflow metadata. Both profiles show broad network egress, so if they share a workspace or operator pipeline, sensitive chatwoot data can flow into Prefect-managed outputs or external calls. The interaction is inferred from docs-only profiles, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF chatwoot exports customer records into a Prefect task input
IF Prefect logs task payloads containing chatwoot messages or orders
IF both agents are granted access to the same shared workspace
mitigations: Separate customer-data and orchestration workspaces
Redact customer fields before handing data to Prefect
Turn off verbose task logging for sensitive payloads
Review outbound integrations on both agents
requires-engineering: add DLP checks on inter-agent transfers

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Chatwoot has broad network egress and API integrations, and Prefect is an orchestration system that can also call external APIs. Even without explicit write scopes, overlapping control of shared mutable resources or the same downstream APIs can create conflicting updates. Because locking and shared-resource details are absent, uncertainty escalates to medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same external system through overlapping APIs
IF Prefect schedules tasks that mutate chatwoot-managed records
IF an operator points both agents at the same mutable dataset
mitigations: Assign separate API credentials per agent
Restrict each agent to disjoint resources
Add a manual approval step before writes
Check for duplicate jobs before enabling automation
requires-engineering: implement resource locking or idempotency keys

D_cascading_error.rationale: Prefect is an orchestration tool, so it can plausibly treat upstream outputs as authoritative, while chatwoot produces customer-facing messages and reports. If chatwoot output is fed into Prefect without verification, Prefect may propagate bad data into downstream workflows. The pairwise pathway is inferred from docs-only profiles, so medium is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF Prefect consumes chatwoot-generated reports without validation
IF chatwoot messages are used as source data for automated Prefect tasks
IF downstream jobs act on unreviewed chatwoot outputs
mitigations: Insert a human review step before orchestration
Validate chatwoot outputs against a schema
Limit Prefect to read-only ingestion for chatwoot data
Flag low-confidence fields for manual review
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data and messages, while Prefect touches workflow metadata only. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to potential policy gaps if customer data is routed through Prefect logs or external calls. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise, but the evidence is sparse.
conditions: IF customer data is written into Prefect logs or artifacts
IF the deployment routes chatwoot data across a jurisdictional boundary
mitigations: Avoid placing customer data in workflow metadata
Shorten log retention for orchestration runs
Review data-processing agreements before enabling transfers
Mask identifiers in task names and parameters
